LESSON: POPULATION STRUCTURE • KENYA • GERMANY

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People and Relationships
Topic 3.4: Population Structure • Kenya • Germany
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 9

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Population Structure • Kenya • Germany, part of People and Relationships in Grade 9 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why is the population structure of a country important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Population Structure • Kenya • Germany together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and Imagination: learners undertake the task of drawing and displaying the age-sex population pyramid of

developed and developing countries (Germany and Kenya).

• Communication and Collaboration: learners work collaboratively as they discuss the significance of population structure in

the distribution of national resources in a society.

Values:
• Unity: learners collaborate with others as they brainstorm on sources of population data.

• Respect: learners appreciate diverse opinions as they brainstorm on sources of population data.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Citizenship: learners acquire knowledge of the population structure of Kenya and Germany together with its influence on the

distribution of resources in society.

• Effective Communication: learners engage a resource person as they discuss factors determining population structure in

Kenya and Germany.

Link to other Learning Areas:

• Learners employ mathematics knowledge to draw and display in class the population structure of Kenya and Germany.

• Learners communicate effectively as they discuss in groups the significance of population structure in the distribution of

national resources in a society helping them develop language skills in English, Kiswahili, and Kenyan Sign Language.
